title: A 350 mm frame move between two satin blocks on a 300 x 300 mm page, as PE-DESIGN 11 writes it to DST
description: Two 39.5 x 6 mm satin blocks (under sewing off) in opposite corners of a 300 x 300 mm Design Page: the move between them is about 211 x 278 mm, longer than one PEC long-form coordinate (204.7 mm) and far longer than a DST record (12.1 mm). Issue #126: how PE-DESIGN splits an over-long move. In its DST the move is 23 jump records of (92, -121) units plus one of (90, -118), i.e. the vector divided evenly into records whose longer axis is the 121-unit maximum; the moves from and to the origin are runs of (-121, 121) records; it never halves. OpenStitch's DST of the same two blocks is compared on the total jump length and the bounds. PE-DESIGN's PES of this design is parked (owner's notes): its PEC writes the move as one trim-flagged long-form jump (-45.5, +168.5 mm) followed by 39 jump records of 7.0 mm in x, which OpenStitch's reader (and a plain 12-bit decode) sums to a different vector from the DST's, so the PEC encoding of a move longer than 204.7 mm is still open.

evidence.note: compat/reference/machine/long-jump-300.dst (PE-DESIGN 11.50, 2026-10-29): 422 records; the inter-block move = 23 jumps of (92,-121) + one of (90,-118); origin runs of 11 x (-121,121) + (-119,119); header +X/-X 1450, +Y/-Y 1450
PE-DESIGN's status bar for the design: 290.00 x 290.00 mm, 372 stitches; Design Settings > Custom Size accepts 100..1000 mm

references.make: Design Settings > Custom Size 300 x 300 mm; a 39.5 x 6 mm satin block (Manual Punch straight block, under sewing off) dragged to the page's top-left corner, Home > Duplicate, the copy dragged to the bottom-right corner (total 290 x 290 mm); App menu > Export, Tajima (*.DST).

measurements.evidence: PE-DESIGN's DST: the same move as jump records of at most 121 units per axis, plus the runs from and to the origin
